statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk of 12% sits in the low band, well below the block threshold.
recommendation: Conditions are described as balanced and two-sided. The narrow flagged window runs from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC (15:30-17:00 Berlin), covering the U.S. cash open and the Richmond Fed / Fed-speaker cluster, with a secondary conditional checkpoint at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and in the 19:00 UTC closing hour. Stress is moderate rather than low, so wider-than-usual intraday ranges are plausible without the persistent no-retracement path that defines the tail case.
headline: Record Nasdaq close, then a fully retraced overnight tape as hike odds firm
body: Nasdaq-100 cash closed Monday at a record 30,482.35, up 2.83% and above 30,000 for the first time, led by an AI chip surge after the reception of Meta's Muse assistant: Arm rose about 17%, Intel about 12%, AMD about 10% through a $1 trillion market capitalisation, Qualcomm more than 9% and Meta about 11%, with the PHLX semiconductor index up 4.3%. Falling crude and softer Treasury yields added support. Overnight the front NQ contract traded up about 0.37% in Asia, as Reuters reported, then gave the move back in full and now sits near 30,783 against a 30,784.75 prior settle, with ES +0.04% and VIX at 14.87. That completed round trip is direct evidence that retracements are still resolving. Offsetting it, the dollar index is near 100.4 at a seven-week high and CME FedWatch October hike odds have risen to 56% from 43.5% a week ago following the Federal Reserve's 16 September increase to 3.75%-4.00%; the 10-year yield is about 4.96% and Brent has bounced 1.8% to about $102.17 after dipping below $100. Tokyo is closed for a public holiday, so Asian depth is light. Cross-asset context from the shared Finviz collection was partial this cycle, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable; its latest-session breadth showed every tracked megacap and semiconductor higher, which is aligned but delayed and is not treated here as live price-path evidence. On the evidence available, mean reversion is functioning and Tail stays low, with conditional risk concentrated in the U.S. cash session.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover a strongly directional U.S. session followed by a calm overnight. From 06:00 UTC on 21 September the mode was trend-up as European and then U.S. buyers extended the AI chip advance; Tail climbed from 11 to a 33 peak at 19:00 UTC while the Nasdaq-100 ran to a 2.83% record close. After the 20:00 UTC cash close volatility decayed quickly, Tail fell to 14 within an hour and to the low teens thereafter, and the mode reverted to normal, where it has stayed through a thin, holiday-shortened Asian session.
outlookSummary: The base case for the next 24 hours is a two-way tape with conditional risk concentrated in the U.S. cash session. Tail is expected to hold the low band through Europe, cross the WATCH threshold at the 13:30 UTC cash open, peak at 24 during the 14:00 UTC Richmond Fed and Fed-speaker cluster, ease afterwards, and re-cross at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and again in the 19:00 UTC closing hour before falling back after the close. That path assumes orderly auction absorption, no disorderly front-end repricing as October hike odds sit at 56%, and no geopolitical discontinuity out of the UN General Assembly week affecting crude. Escalation beyond the flagged window would require observed one-way structure: shallow or failed retracements with the index holding near session extremes.
